arxiv-2011-07389.title: Words are the Window to the Soul: Language-based User Representations for Fake News Detection
arxiv-2011-07389.creator: Marco Del Tredici, Raquel Fernández
arxiv-2011-07389.description: Abstract Cognitive and social traits of individuals are reflected in language use. Moreover, individuals who are prone to spread fake news online often share common traits. Building on these ideas, we introduce a model that creates representations of individuals on social media based only on the language they produce, and use them to detect fake news.

arxiv-2303-14475.title: An Informed Neural Network for Discovering Historical Documentation assisting the Repatriation of Indigenous Ancestral Human Remains
arxiv-2303-14475.creator: Md Abul Bashar \affilnum 1, Richi Nayak \affilnum 1, Gareth Knapman \affilnum 2, Paul Turnbull \affilnum 2,3, Cressida Fforde \affilnum 2

Among the pressing issues facing Australian and other First Nations peoples is the repatriation of the bodily remains of their ancestors, which are currently held in Western scientific institutions.

Bielewicz, A. Blondel, M. Bogomilov, Y. Bondar, N. Bostan, A. Brandin, W. Bryliński, J. Brzychczyk, M. Buryakov, A.F. Camino, M. Ćirković
arxiv-2306-02961.description: Abstract This paper presents multiplicity measurements of charged hadrons produced in 120 GeV/ c c proton-carbon interactions. The measurements were made using data collected at the NA61/SHINE experiment during two different data-taking periods, with increased phase space coverage in the second configuration due to the addition of new subdetectors.

arxiv-2409-00471.title: Ejective feedback as a quenching mechanism in the 1.5 billion years of the universe: detection of neutral gas outflow in a z = 4 z=4 recently quenched galaxy
arxiv-2409-00471.creator: Po-Feng Wu
arxiv-2409-00471.description: Abstract The confirmation of massive quiescent galaxies emerging within the first billion years of the universe poses intriguing questions about the mechanisms of galaxy formation. There must be highly efficient processes at work to shut down star formation in galaxies at cosmic dawn.

arxiv-2412-03438.title: The relation of galaxies and dark matter haloes to the filamentary cosmic web 2024 The relation of galaxies and dark matter haloes to the filamentary cosmic web – References
arxiv-2412-03438.creator: Navdha, Philipp Busch, Simon D. M. White
arxiv-2412-03438.description: Abstract We use the Millennium Simulation to study the relation of galaxies and dark matter haloes to the cosmic web. We define the web as the unique, fully connected, percolating object with (unsmoothed) matter density everywhere exceeding 5.25 times the cosmic mean. This object contains 35% of all cosmic mass but occupies only 0.62% of all cosmic volume.

arxiv-2505-23271.title: LADA: Scalable Label-Specific CLIP Adapter for Continual Learning
arxiv-2505-23271.creator: Mao-Lin Luo, Zi-Hao Zhou, Tong Wei, Min-Ling Zhang
arxiv-2505-23271.description: Abstract Continual learning with vision-language models like CLIP offers a pathway toward scalable machine learning systems by leveraging its transferable representations. Existing CLIP-based methods adapt the pre-trained image encoder by adding multiple sets of learnable parameters, with each task using a partial set of parameters.

pmc-11009551.title: Postpartum lifestyle behaviour among women with prior gestational diabetes mellitus: evidence from the HUNT study
pmc-11009551.creator: Hanne Ringvoll, Marit Kolberg, Vegar Rangul, Ingrid Hafskjold, Eirin Beate Haug, Rune Blomhoff, Hege Berg Henriksen, Julie Horn
pmc-11009551.description: IntroductionWomen with a history of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) are at increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and cardiovascular disease (CVD). Recommendations for postpartum follow-up include targeted lifestyle advice to lower the risk.The aim of this study was to compare postpartum lifestyle behaviours and perceptions among women with and without a history of GDM.

pmc-11538000.title: Pyroptosis regulation by Salmonella effectors
pmc-11538000.creator: Yuan Meng, Qianjin Zhang, Mengen Xu, Ke Ding, Zuhua Yu, Jing Li
pmc-11538000.description: The genus Salmonella contains the most common foodborne pathogens frequently isolated from food-producing animals and is responsible for zoonotic infections in humans and animals. Salmonella infection in humans and animals can cause intestinal damage, resulting in intestinal inflammation and disruption of intestinal homeostasis more severe cases can lead to bacteremia.

pmc-12745157.title: Exploring the mechanism of Heidihuang Pill in the treatment of osteoporosis based on network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation
pmc-12745157.creator: Zenghui Tian, Kaiying Cui, Yuxiao Tian, Yungang Chen, Guoyan Liu, Farong Zhang, Yanke Hao, Yingying Li
pmc-12745157.description: BackgroundCurrently, anti-osteoporosis (OP) treatment imposes a certain economic burden on patients and society; therefore, studies have focused on exploring anti-OP therapies. As a classic prescription in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), the Heidihuang Pill (HP) was clinically shown to alleviate OP. However, the mechanism behind its effect remains unclear.

pmc-13070412.title: Liposomal Co-Delivery of Antigenic Glycan LDNF and α-GalCer Elicits Potent IgG Responses with Potential for Anti-Helminth Immunity
pmc-13070412.creator: Qianghui Tang, Qiang Chao, Jianfeng Zhang, Bei Wang, Song Zhao, Kun Yang
pmc-13070412.description: IntroductionParasitic worms (helminths) express unique antigenic glycans such as LDN and LDNF, which are absent in mammalian hosts and represent promising vaccine targets. However, free glycans typically elicit weak immune responses and require multivalent delivery and adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity and promote antibody class-switching.

pmc-13100908.title: Origins of the selectivity of late transition metals of Group 9 and Group 10 for oxidative addition of C–H vs. C–Cl bonds
pmc-13100908.creator: Yehao Qiu, Alistair J. Sterling, Kevin K. Ikeda, Alexander Zech, Matthias Loipersberger, Diptarka Hait, Martin Head-Gordon, John F. Hartwig
pmc-13100908.description: Oxidative addition of carbon–hydrogen or carbon–halogen bonds occurs in many reactions catalyzed by late transition-metal complexes. Metals of Group 9 typically react with C–H bonds faster than C–X bonds, while those of Group 10 react with C–X bonds faster than C–H bonds.

pmc-13226893.title: Effect of monochromatic light combinations on muscle fiber types in broilers after thyroidectomy
pmc-13226893.creator: Yameng Liu, Zixu Wang, Jing Cao, Yulan Dong, Ting Gao, Fuwei Li, Enliang Song, Yaoxing Chen
pmc-13226893.description: Our previous research indicated that monochromatic light combinations influence muscle fiber types in broilers, potentially through alterations in thyroid function, yet the underlying mechanisms remained elusive. Here, we employed a thyroidectomy (TX) model to investigate the role of thyroid hormone (T3) in mediating these light-induced effects.

pmc-13424985.title: Patient awareness and perception of cardiovascular risk in rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases: results from an international survey
pmc-13424985.creator: Alessia Alunno, Javier Rodríguez-Carrio, Sander van Leuven, Valentin Ritschl, Valentina Schmolik, Peter Böhm, Francesca Marchiori, Karen Schreiber, Dina Husum, Tanja Stamm, Gabriella Szucs, Fabiola Atzeni, Zoltan Szekanecz, Michael Nurmohamed, EULAR Cardiovascular in inflammatory arthritis (CVIIA) S
pmc-13424985.description: ObjectivesInflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases (RMDs) are hallmarked by an increased risk of cardiovascular (CV) disease compared with the general population. Evidence suggests that CV risk remains under-recognised and underdiscussed in routine care, although data on patient experience is lacking. We aimed to assess awareness, perceptions, and experiences regarding CV risk and prevention in patients with RMDs.

pmc-13584661.title: From environmental heterogeneity to stability: Beta‐diversity stabilizes biomass across space
pmc-13584661.creator: Benedikt Brunner, James G. Hagan, Jesper Hassellöv, Julia Mari Murata, Lara Colaço Martins, Pedro de La Patelliere, Elena Schrofner‐Brunner, Lars Gamfeldt
pmc-13584661.description: Understanding how biodiversity influences ecosystem stability across heterogeneous landscapes is a central challenge in ecology. The spatial insurance hypothesis proposes that turnover in species composition stabilizes ecosystem processes in heterogeneous environments if species dominate in the habitats to which they are best adapted. Yet, empirical evidence remains mixed, partly due to confounding factors and overlooked causal mechanisms.

pmc-13631602.title: Uterine angiomatosis as an unexpected cause of refractory pelvic pain and heavy menstrual bleeding: a case report and literature review
pmc-13631602.creator: Zubaydah Abdi, Sadia Zare, Ruth Grundy, Alexander Polson, Salwa Idle
pmc-13631602.description: Angiomatosis is a rare benign vascular lesion characterised by diffuse, haphazard proliferation of blood vessels, most commonly within adipose and fibrous tissue. This report describes the case of a patient in her early 30s who presented with refractory menorrhagia and pelvic pain. Following total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy, histopathological examination identified angiomatosis of the uterine corpus and cervix.
